{
  "candidate_rtl": "module comparator_16bit (
    input [15:0] A,
    input [15:0] B,
    output gt,
    output eq,
    output lt
);
    wire [3:0] group_eq;
    wire [3:0] group_gt;

    genvar k;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : compare_groups
            assign group_eq[k] = (A[4*k +: 4] == B[4*k +: 4]);
            assign group_gt[k] = (A[4*k +: 4] > B[4*k +: 4]);
        end
    endgenerate

    assign eq = &group_eq;
    assign gt = group_gt[3]
              | (group_eq[3] & group_gt[2])
              | (group_eq[3] & group_eq[2] & group_gt[1])
              | (group_eq[3] & group_eq[2] & group_eq[1] & group_gt[0]);
    assign lt = ~(gt | eq);
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original independently expressed full-width magnitude comparisons can produce long comparison paths and duplicate ordering logic.",
  "rewrite": "Compare four unsigned 4-bit slices in parallel, then combine their results with an explicit most-significant-group-first lookahead expression. Share group equality with the equality output and derive less-than from the mutually exclusive greater-than and equality results.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The grouped lookahead exposes parallel local comparisons and a shallow global decision network. A timing improvement is expected if the original mapping uses a deeper comparison structure; the actual gain requires the specified mapping and STA flow. The less-than output adds a final NOR stage.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Eliminates the separate full-width less-than comparator, providing area headroom for the lookahead network. Exact mapped area, compliance with the area cap, and zero slew/capacitance violations remain unverified without running the evaluation flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module name, ports, widths, unsigned interpretation, and purely combinational behavior. For all binary 16-bit A and B, the highest unequal 4-bit group determines unsigned ordering. Since unsigned ordering is total, lt = ~(gt | eq) exactly matches A < B. No parameters, state, assumptions, dependencies, or undefined outputs are introduced."
}
